output = []

for item in _items:
    data = dict(item["json"])
    html = str(data.get("html") or "")

    if not html:
        continue

    escaped_html = (
        html.replace("&", "&")
        .replace('"', """)
        .replace("<", "<")
        .replace(">", ">")
    )

    data["embed_code"] = (
        '<iframe title="Rosebud Village email preview" '
        'sandbox="" '
        'style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:720px;'
        'height:1400px;margin:0 auto;border:0;" '
        'srcdoc="' + escaped_html + '"></iframe>'
    )

    output.append({"json": data})

return output

nodes.name: Code to convert email as a webpage preview

parameters.text:
Create a reusable HTML section for a monthly “What’s on” webpage for Rosebud Retirement Village, Victoria. This HTML will be generated by an n8n workflow on the first day of each month and embedded into an existing webpage.

INPUTS
The workflow supplies:

1. The target month and year: 
2. Events for that month, including event title, summary sentence, village, location within the village, date, marketing approval status and more-information URL.
3. Image rows from the Google Sheets tab “Images for each Village location”, including village location, image description and direct image URL.
4. The existing approved HTML as a design reference.

CONTENT
- Include only Rosebud events occurring in the target month that have been approved by marketing
- maximum of 105 words
- Feature a selection of highlights in warm, welcoming, community-focused prose.
- Mention each activity only once, including recurring activities.
- Write in Australian English.
- Do not invent events, dates or details.
- Use the supplied target month dynamically. The heading should read “Hello, [Month].”
- Divide the copy into three short paragraphs: an opening introduction, mentioning something about the season or events in that month, activity highlights, and a closing invitation to visit the village or join one of the activites
- Match the approved example’s tone and approximate length.

DESIGN
- Preserve the approved “Flowing story” design.
- Match the fonts and colour palette of https://www.rosebudvillage.com/.
- Use Austin for the large serif text and Whitney for supporting text, retaining the font sources in the supplied HTML.
- Background: #FDFAF7.
- Main text: #5A6457.
- Event links: #52844F.
- Hover text: #2B5336.
- Hover highlight background: #E7ECDF.
- Main paragraph text: approximately 34px on desktop and 26px on mobile.
- Keep the image smaller than the main text block, floated to the right on desktop so the text flows around it.
- Make the layout responsive and stack the image and text appropriately on mobile.
- Scope all CSS and JavaScript to a unique section ID so the embed does not affect the surrounding webpage.
- Do not add duplicate site navigation or a site-wide header or footer.

IMAGES AND INTERACTION
- On initial page load, display the image labelled “Hero image” in the image tab.
- Initially show a brief welcome caption. Hide the “Learn more” link until an event is selected.
- Make event names green and underlined.
- When a visitor hovers over, focuses on or taps an event name:
  1. Update the image to the image associated with that event’s location within the village.
  2. Display that event’s summary sentence immediately beneath the image.
  3. Append a hyperlinked “Learn more” at the end of the summary sentence.
  4. Set “Learn more” to that event’s more-information URL.
- If an image has already been assigned to another featured event, use a different unused image from the supplied image list. Prefer an image relevant to the activity.
- Reserve the Hero image for the initial page-load state.
- If there are insufficient suitable images, reuse a relevant image rather than inventing an image URL.
- Keep the selected image and summary visible when the pointer leaves the event name, so visitors can move to “Learn more”.
- Give “Learn more” the same text colour, underline and background highlight on hover and keyboard focus as the event names.
- Prevent image and caption changes from causing disruptive layout shifts.
- Provide meaningful image alt text and keyboard-accessible interactions.
- Use supplied image URLs directly. Do not generate images.
- If an event has no more-information URL, use a clearly marked placeholder anchor; do not invent a real destination.

MONTHLY OPERATION
- The n8n trigger runs on the first day of each month using the Australia/Melbourne timezone.
- Generate content for the month beginning of the following month.
- Use the target month and year supplied by n8n. Never hard-code a month, year or event list.
- Assume n8n reads the current spreadsheet data and supplies it on each run.
- Produce a complete replacement HTML section each month.
- Do not include scheduling logic, Google credentials or spreadsheet API calls in the webpage code.

OUTPUT
Return only the ready-to-embed HTML fragment, with scoped CSS and JavaScript included.
Do not include Markdown code fences, explanations or setup instructions.
Validate that the event-to-image mappings, summaries, links, Hero initial state and hover/focus/tap interactions are consistent before returning the HTML. {{ $json['Start date'] }}
